correctness.rationale: All nonzero elements of a finite acyclic graph inverse semigroup have unique equal-terminal path-pair forms. The prefix multiplication law, acyclic incomparability of distinct equal-terminal paths, and equality-of-normal-form argument prove that two nonidempotents cannot have an equal nonzero product; the remaining disjoint zero-product and common-prefix cases yield exact individual centralizers. Double-counting prefix-comparable pairs gives B_vw and the full stated K(E) vertex-matrix polynomial with diagonal and shared-prefix corrections. The standalone checker uses actual products and exhaustively passes 1099 simple acyclic graphs, 681 bounded acyclic multigraphs and four regression examples; tests corroborate the general proof, not replace it. The theorem covers parallel edges, isolated vertices, and empty path conventions.

value.rationale: All-element centralizer cardinalities and ordered commuting-pair counts are fundamental semigroup invariants. Graph inverse semigroups can contain exponentially many path pairs even when the defining acyclic graph has few vertices. Replacing explicit pairwise multiplication with a graph path-count matrix formula gives a genuinely useful exact computation, covers arbitrary parallel edges/isolated vertices, and exposes the nontrivial cross-class/common-prefix effects that are invisible from separate Brandt classes.
